title: Foggy glasses at lunch
setting: Lunchtime at a small café near the office. Mai has a cold and turns up in a mask, and every breath fogs up her glasses. She sits down across from Yuki while they wait for their food.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mai, kotchi kotchi! are, masuku shiteru. kaze hiita no?
lines.ja: マイ、こっちこっち！あれ、マスクしてる。風邪ひいたの？
lines.kana: まい、こっちこっち！あれ、マスクしてる。かぜひいたの？
lines.english: Mai, over here! Oh, you're wearing a mask. Have you caught a cold?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, chotto nodo ga itakute. demo masuku suru to, megane ga sugu kumoru n da yo ne.
lines.ja: うん、ちょっと喉が痛くて。でもマスクすると、眼鏡がすぐ曇るんだよね。
lines.kana: うん、ちょっとのどがいたくて。でもマスクすると、めがねがすぐくもるんだよね。
lines.english: Yeah, my throat's a bit sore. But whenever I wear a mask, my glasses fog up right away.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: aa, sore, megane kaketeru hito wa minna iu yo ne.
lines.ja: ああ、それ、眼鏡かけてる人はみんな言うよね。
lines.kana: ああ、それ、めがねかけてるひとはみんないうよね。
lines.english: Oh, everyone who wears glasses says that.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: hora, ima mo. mae ga zenzen mienai.
lines.ja: ほら、今も。前が全然見えない。
lines.kana: ほら、いまも。まえがぜんぜんみえない。
lines.english: See, it's happening right now. I can't see a thing.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, masuku hazushitara? koko, hito sukunai shi.
lines.ja: じゃあ、マスク外したら？ここ、人少ないし。
lines.kana: じゃあ、マスクはずしたら？ここ、ひとすくないし。
lines.english: Then why not take your mask off? There aren't many people in here.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: uun, yuki ni kaze utsuttara iya da kara, masuku wa shitoku.
lines.ja: ううん、ユキに風邪うつったら嫌だから、マスクはしとく。
lines.kana: ううん、ゆきにかぜうつったらいやだから、マスクはしとく。
lines.english: No, I'd hate for you to catch my cold, so I'll keep it on.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, megane no hou o hazushitara?
lines.ja: じゃあ、眼鏡のほうを外したら？
lines.kana: じゃあ、めがねのほうをはずしたら？
lines.english: Then how about taking your glasses off instead?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: megane hazusu to nanimo mienai n da kedo, maa, ii ka. hazushitoku.
lines.ja: 眼鏡外すと何も見えないんだけど、まあ、いいか。外しとく。
lines.kana: めがねはずすとなにもみえないんだけど、まあ、いいか。はずしとく。
lines.english: I can't see a thing without my glasses, but oh well. I'll take them off for now.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, zenzen. a, asoko, tanaka-san ja nai? tanaka-san, otsukaresama desu!
lines.ja: うん、全然。あ、あそこ、田中さんじゃない？田中さん、お疲れさまです！
lines.kana: うん、ぜんぜん。あ、あそこ、たなかさんじゃない？たなかさん、おつかれさまです！
lines.english: Yeah, totally. Oh, isn't that Tanaka-san over there? Hi, Tanaka-san!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: chotto, mai! hayaku megane kakete! ano hito, tanaka-san ja nai yo.
lines.ja: ちょっと、マイ！早く眼鏡かけて！あの人、田中さんじゃないよ。
lines.kana: ちょっと、まい！はやくめがねかけて！あのひと、たなかさんじゃないよ。
lines.english: Mai, wait! Put your glasses on, quick! That's not Tanaka-san.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, uso! megane, megane. a, honto da. zenzen chigau hito da.
lines.ja: え、うそ！眼鏡、眼鏡。あ、ほんとだ。全然違う人だ。
lines.kana: え、うそ！めがね、めがね。あ、ほんとだ。ぜんぜんちがうひとだ。
lines.english: What, no way! Glasses, where are my glasses? Oh, you're right. That's someone else entirely.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ano hito, metcha bikkuri shiteta yo. mou megane hazushicha dame.
lines.ja: あの人、めっちゃびっくりしてたよ。もう眼鏡外しちゃだめ。
lines.kana: あのひと、めっちゃびっくりしてたよ。もうめがねはずしちゃだめ。
lines.english: He looked so startled. No more taking your glasses off.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: hazukashii. demo, masuku shitetara, mata kumoru yo.
lines.ja: 恥ずかしい。でも、マスクしてたら、また曇るよ。
lines.kana: はずかしい。でも、マスクしてたら、またくもるよ。
lines.english: So embarrassing. But as long as I've got the mask on, they'll just fog up again.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, gohan kita yo. hora, masuku hazushite.
lines.ja: あ、ご飯来たよ。ほら、マスク外して。
lines.kana: あ、ごはんきたよ。ほら、マスクはずして。
lines.english: Oh, the food's here. Come on, take your mask off.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sou da ne. masuku hazushitara, megane kakete mo kumoranai. yatto yuki no kao ga mieta!
lines.ja: そうだね。マスク外したら、眼鏡かけても曇らない。やっとユキの顔が見えた！
lines.kana: そうだね。マスクはずしたら、めがねかけてもくもらない。やっとゆきのかおがみえた！
lines.english: True. With the mask off, my glasses don't fog up. At last I can see your face!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: yokatta. kono hanashi, ato de tanaka-san ni hanasou kana.
lines.ja: よかった。この話、あとで田中さんに話そうかな。
lines.kana: よかった。このはなし、あとでたなかさんにはなそうかな。
lines.english: Good. Maybe I'll tell Tanaka-san this story later.

choices.english: Mai takes her mask off so her glasses stop fogging up, and then Tanaka-san walks in and sees her.
Yuki doesn't recognise Mai at first, because Mai is wearing a mask and glasses.
Mai takes off her fogged-up glasses, and without them she greets a stranger, thinking he's Tanaka-san.

questions.explanation: Lines 2-8: Mai's mask keeps fogging up her glasses. She won't take the mask off in case Yuki catches her cold (line 6), so she takes her glasses off instead. In line 10 she calls out to 'Tanaka-san', and in lines 11-12 Yuki makes her put her glasses back on: it's someone else entirely. A is wrong because Mai only takes the mask off when the food arrives (lines 15-16), and the real Tanaka-san never turns up. B is wrong because Yuki spots Mai straight away and calls her over (line 1).

questions.english: When Yuki first suggests taking the mask off, what does Mai say she'll do with it?
questions.ja: マイさんは、マスクをどうすると言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、マスクをどうするといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, masuku o dou suru to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I'll keep wearing the mask (with kiru, as for a shirt).
I'll hang on to the mask (keep it with me).

questions.explanation: Line 6: Mai says masuku wa shitoku (shite oku, leave it on), and Yuki noticed it in line 1 with masuku shiteru. Small things you wear, like a mask or a watch, take suru. A, kiru, is where English 'wear' points, but kiru is for clothes you put your body into, like a shirt or jacket (fuku o kiru), not a mask. C, motte oku, means keeping the mask with you, in your hand or your bag, not on your face.

questions.english: Yuki holds up her phone and says: "OK, I'm taking the photo. Look this way!" You've still got your mask on. Ask her to wait while you take it off.
questions.ja: じゃあ、写真撮るよ。こっち見て！
questions.kana: じゃあ、しゃしんとるよ。こっちみて！
questions.romaji: jaa, shashin toru yo. kotchi mite!
questions.answer: Ask her to wait while you take your mask off, using hazusu: chotto matte, masuku hazusu kara.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, chotto matte. masuku hazusu kara.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、ちょっと待って。マスク外すから。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, hang on. Let me take my mask off.

modelAnswers.ja: 待って、マスク外してもいい？
modelAnswers.english: Wait, is it OK if I take my mask off?

questions.explanation: A mask comes off with hazusu, as in Yuki's masuku hazushitara? (line 5) and masuku hazushite (line 15). Don't say nugu: that's for clothes and shoes. Casual toru works too (masuku toru kara), but masuku totte on its own can sound like 'pass me a mask'. Putting it back on afterwards is suru again: mata masuku suru.

questions.english: Mai complains that her mask fogs up her glasses. Yuki says a certain kind of person always says that. Who does she mean?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、どんな人がみんなそう言うと言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、どんなひとがみんなそういうといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, donna hito ga minna sou iu to iimashita ka?

choices.english: People who are just putting their glasses on.
People who keep their glasses hooked on their shirt.

questions.explanation: Line 3: megane kaketeru hito. kakeru is the verb for glasses, and kaketeru describes a state, so this simply means people who wear glasses. It's a way of describing someone. B reads -teru as an action happening right now, but Yuki means glasses-wearers in general, who all complain about masks fogging their lenses. C: kakeru does literally mean 'hang', which is why it goes with glasses (they hang on your ears), but megane kaketeru means they're on your face, not hooked on your clothes.

questions.english: You're having ramen with Kenta. The steam hits his face and he groans: "Ugh, my glasses have fogged up and I can't see a thing." Suggest he take them off while he eats.
questions.ja: ああ、眼鏡曇って、全然見えない。
questions.kana: ああ、めがねくもって、ぜんぜんみえない。
questions.answer: Suggest he take them off with hazusu, the same verb as for a mask: jaa, megane hazushitara?

modelAnswers.english: Then why don't you take your glasses off?

modelAnswers.romaji: taberu toki wa, megane hazushita hou ga ii yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 食べる時は、眼鏡外したほうがいいよ。
modelAnswers.english: You'd better take your glasses off while you eat.

questions.explanation: Yuki does exactly this in line 7 (megane no hou o hazushitara?), and Mai answers megane hazusu to nanimo mienai (line 8). Glasses and masks share hazusu for taking off, but not for putting on: a mask takes suru, glasses take kakeru (line 16, megane kakete mo kumoranai). Not megane o nugu: nugu is for things you're dressed in, like clothes and shoes.

newWords.english: fog up, mist over (glasses); also cloud over (the sky)
can see, be visible (mienai = can't see, mieta = could see)
